sentences: Vaudeville dancers the dancer and his wife the woman are barely getting by on her job at a dance hall.
He anxiously awaits her return from work, where she is often delayed by a generously tipping customer she calls "the gift-giver", who turns out to be police detective the detective.
Depressed and anxious, the dancer impulsively throws his only pair of tap dancing shoes at howling cats outside his window.
When he immediately searches for them, he cannot find them, but they mysteriously reappear outside the apartment door the next morning.
The old man, a reclusive old neighbor rumored to have a large stash of old, high-value currency, is found murdered, and the dancer's shoe prints are found at the scene.
Unaware of the killing, the dancer finds a wallet containing two thousand dollars in old bills.
He wants to turn them in to the police, but the woman persuades him to wait and see if anyone places an ad in the newspaper.
After three days, they decide to spend some of the money, $200.00 each.
As a result, he is arrested for the murder.
The dancer is convicted and sentenced to death.
His wife implores the detective to help her find the real killer.
The suspect, a former boarder at the same house, has also spent a large amount of money, which he claims he inherited from his recently deceased mother.
The detective does not believe him and takes him into custody, but he later proves to have a solid alibi.
As the hours tick down to the dancer's midnight execution, the detective makes it clear to the woman that he is obsessed with her.
He reveals that he purchased a fancy apartment and furnished it just for her.
The detective claims he paid for it with his entire life savings.
When the woman rebuffs him, he angrily reaches into his pocket, throws one last tip into her lap, and starts to leave.
The woman sees that it is an old note and realizes that he is the murderer.
She appears to change her mind and agrees to go see the apartment with him, but manages to call the police first.
At the apartment, she gets him to confess what he has done, and the listening policemen emerge from hiding.
When he goes for his gun, they are forced to shoot him dead.
As the nephew visits his uncle, the judge, in the city, he is knocked unconscious by an unknown attacker.
When he wakes up, the nephew finds out that his uncle has been stabbed to death.
The judge's private secretary, the secretary, finds the two men and calls the police to the scene.
When the nephew wakes up he has the knife that stabbed his uncle in his hand.
In another part of the city, the young man and his chauffeur the driver, discover a man trying to burglar his way into a house as they are walking home from the movies.
They make a citizens arrest of the man, who turns out to be the house owner, district attorney the prosecutor, trying to climb in through the window.
The young man, who is the son of private detective the sleuth, and his chauffeur are put in jail because of their unlawful action.

The prosecutor is head of investigating the judge's murder, and hears from the judge's butler, the servant, that the nephew wasn't allowed into the judge's home, and had to climb in through the window in the same way the prosecutor did.
In an interview with the police, the secretary also tells them that the nephew, who is her boyfriend, argued with the judge about the purchase the nephew had made of some stock worth $30,000.
The secretary also heard how the judge contacted his lawyer the attorney and asked for a meet the following day, in order to update his will, to exclude the nephew.
This information gives the nephew the most plausible motive for murdering the judge.
Famous detective the sleuth visits the prosecutor, his old acquaintance, to apologize for his son and the driver and their behavior the other night.
At his visit, the sleuth overhears that two sets of fingerprints were found on the knife used to kill the judge; one set belonging to the nephew and one to hardened criminal the convict.
The sleuth happens to know that the convict was executed for another murder at the prison six months earlier.
The convict got his death sentence from the judge.
The sleuth is then asked by police investigator the officer to help the police out on the case.
When district attorney the prosecutor is shot and killed soon after, the convict's fingerprints are again found on the scene, on the prosecutor's desk.
While investigating the case at the judge's office, the sleuth and the officer catch the judge's clerk the assistant looking through the judge's files.
The two men also find out that the attorney, the judge's attorney, defended the convict in the trial which ultimately sent him to the electric chair.
From the judge's documents they find that the attorney is also working on a commission against racketeering.

A letter addressed to the nephew, to be opened in case the judge died, states that the judge had found evidence that the convict may have been innocent of the murder for which he was convicted, and that the prosecutor was to be informed of this.
The sleuth and the officer go to find the convict's buried body, but finds his coffin has been dug up and removed.

Fearing that the convict's murder trial is connected to the judge's murder and racketeering, the sleuth sees to it that all the jurors involved in the ruling are taken into protective custody for the time being.
They locate everyone but one, the juror, who is attacked in his home and killed before the policemen get there.
The convict's fingerprints are once again found on the murder scene.
The sleuth looks into the fingerprints and learns that it is in fact possible to forge someone else's prints.
He gathers the secretary, the nephew and the attorney at the judge's home to confront them about the fake fingerprints.
When all are gathered in the judge's study, the power is cut and everything turns dark.
They are locked in by an unknown man holding a gun, but manage to break out again, and find all documents related to the racketeering, insurance fraud and the convict gone.
The sleuth discovers that the convict has a brother, the sibling, who got a letter from the convict when he was in jail, saying he was about to be sentenced to death for a murder he didn't commit.
The sleuth tells everyone that the sibling, to revenge his brother, was planning on killing everyone involved in the wrong sentencing of his brother, and dug up his brother's coffin.
While the sleuth explains this, the sibling enters the room with a gun and explains that his real purpose for digging up the coffin was simply to give his brother a proper burial.
The sibling is then overpowered by the attorney, who grabs the sibling's gun.

The sleuth goes on to explain the real murderer is the attorney, because he was involved in an insurance scam with the convict and wanted all the money for himself, thus framing the convict for a murder to get rid of him.
The attorney, sure to get away now that he has a gun, explains how he copied the convict's prints to lead the police on a false trail.
The sleuth tells the attorney that the gun isn't loaded, since he gave it to the sibling earlier, and that it was all part of a set-up.
The attorney tries to flee but is stopped by the driver and arrested.
The manager manages the (real-life) wrestler, the champion.

Taking a special interest in the champion's match is a police lieutenant, the policeman, who is keeping an eye on everybody: mobster the gangster, his moll the girlfriend and another wrestling star, the rival, who is dating the manager.
A quarrel between the wrestlers erupts and the policeman suggests they settle it in the ring.
So much publicity ensues that the match is televised live.
The rival is confident he will win, as is the girlfriend, who requests his autograph.
The rival is getting the better of the champion for a while, but is suddenly pinned, defeated and does not get up.
The champion is clearly the prime suspect if this is a murder, while the policeman gets in hot water at the police department for proposing the match in the first place.
The gangster is the detective's best guess as the culprit until he views a rebroadcast of the whole evening on TV.
He finds the pen the girlfriend used to get the rival's autograph and realizes what happened: It's been poisoned.
The much-valued famous diamond is looted during its opening showcase.
A suspicious inspector suspects reformed jewel thief and current private detective the sleuth, alias the "loner," to be the perpetrator and promptly arrests him.
In actuality, the true masterminds are the first thief and the second thief.
An eagle-eyed servant, the sleuth's butler, spots the two criminals' hideout.
It is revealed that they are involved with precious stone cutter the craftsman.
Nearby news anchor the reporter decides to join the servant and the loner, who has evaded capture, in storming the jewel thieves' hiding spot.
The first thief and the second thief are handcuffed but in the middle of the scuffle, the famous diamond is accidentally flung out of the window.
Upon retrieval by the reporter, the jewel is found to be a fake.
The sleuth deduces that the craftsman took away the real diamond and has the police capture him.
Portly private detective the investigator is asked by dental nurse the assistant to investigate the unexplained murder of her boss.
Suspicion falls on disappeared patient the missing man, last seen being driven from his appointment by the chauffeur of probable gangster the mobster.
The investigator contacts the ex-wife, the missing man's former lover and briefly his wife, who reveals that the missing man had once spent time in jail.
The police tell the investigator that the missing man's offense was the theft of half a million dollars, money that was not recovered.
In jail, the missing man had a cellmate named the performer, a circus clown, with whom he shared many secrets.
On release, the performer had claimed the missing man's share of the loot from the mobster, the heist's organizer, in order to fulfil his ambition to own his own circus.
The performer's side of the deal was to eliminate the missing man, and he left the corpse in a truck that was destroyed by fire.
When he realized that the missing man had undergone dental treatment, creating dental records that could be used to identify him, the performer killed the dentist and the assistant.
The investigator locates the performer, and in a final shootout, the performer is fatally wounded and dies in his own circus ring.
On the coast of the county, young the heir is raised by his older, wealthy cousin the guardian on a large estate.
When the weather threatens the guardian's health, he moves to the foreign city, leaving the heir behind with his godfather the family friend.
In the foreign city, the guardian decides to marry his cousin the woman.
However, back in the county, the heir receives disturbing letters from the guardian, complaining of the woman's treatment as well as that of his physicians.
The family friend believes that the guardian is of unsound mind and may have inherited his dead father's brain tumor.

The heir travels to the foreign city and meets the adviser, who informs him that the guardian has died of a brain tumor, producing a death certificate as proof, and that the guardian's will left the county estate to the heir upon his 25th birthday.
The woman, who left the foreign city the day before the heir arrived, has inherited nothing and has no claim on the estate.
The heir suspects the woman of murder and vows revenge.
Months later, the woman visits the county and the heir invites her to the house.
He discovers she is different from what he had imagined: beautiful, ladylike and kind.

When she intends to leave, he shows her the guardian's letters and admits that he planned to accuse her of wrongdoing, but as he no longer suspects her, he throws the letters in the fireplace to demonstrate his faith in her.
He later instructs his executor, the family friend, to award the woman a generous allowance of £5,000 per year, suggesting that the money is hers anyway.
The woman responds with gratitude and warmth and stays at the estate for an extended period, despite gossip.

Yet when the family friend tells the heir that the woman has overdrawn her accounts and she was notorious for "loose" living in the foreign city, the heir rejects the family friend's warnings and instead cedes the entire estate to the woman on his 25th birthday.
When the day arrives, he solicits from her a vague romantic promise, which she gives, and they passionately kiss.
However, the next day when the heir announces to his friends that he and the woman are engaged to be wed, the woman dismisses the announcement as lunacy.
The woman later tells the heir that her promise did not mean marriage, that she will never marry him and she only showed him love the because of the wealth that has given her.
Emotionally devastated, the heir succumbs to bouts of fever and delirium, but the woman nurses him back to health.
In his fever, the heir imagines a wedding with the woman and awakens three weeks later convinced they are married and surprised to hear that she intends to return to the foreign city.
Before she leaves, the heir becomes convinced that the woman is attempting to poison him and that she had indeed murdered the guardian.
So great is his anger toward the woman that he neglects to warn her about a footbridge in need of repair at the edge of the estate.
Instead, the heir and his friend the confidante secretly rummage through the woman's room for a letter from the adviser, assuming that it will incriminate the woman.
Instead, upon discovering and reading the letter, they learn that the adviser merely discussed the woman's affections for the heir and suggests that she bring the heir when visiting the foreign city.
The heir finds that the woman has indeed suffered a fatal accident while crossing the unrepaired footbridge.
With her last words, she asks the heir why he did not warn her of the danger.
She then dies, leaving the heir to wonder for the rest of his life about his own guilt about the death of the innocent woman.
On an ocean liner sailing from the city, the husband lifts his bride the heiress over the threshold of cabin B16, where the maid, a stewardess busy with finishing touches, greets them and withdraws.
The heiress has been unsettled by her father's recent death; she and the husband have had a whirlwind courtship of just four weeks.
The husband suggests the heiress go on deck to enjoy the ship's departure while he takes fifteen minutes to see the purser to deposit money for safekeeping.
As the heiress waves to the crowd in excitement, fellow passenger the other woman asks the heiress who is seeing her off.
The heiress replies that she is waving to no one in particular, as she is traveling with her husband.
The couple had agreed to meet in one of the ship's bars but the husband fails to show up.
After waiting for over an hour, the heiress visits the purser and discovers that the husband has not been there.
Returning to her cabin, she finds it locked and the attending steward insists that cabin B16 has not been booked for this trip.
She is registered solo under her maiden name, the heiress's former name, in cabin B18, where her luggage is found, but not the husband's.
Insisting on seeing cabin B16, the heiress finds no sign of having previously been there.
She cannot produce her ticket or passport because these are in the husband's possession.
Since they were married only the day before, she is not wearing a wedding ring and her luggage still bears tags with her maiden name.
Under stress, she faints, and the ship's physician, the doctor, embarks on a search for the facts.
The maid insists she never saw the heiress or the husband.

While boarding the husband had fallen back in the crowd going up the gangplank and was briefly separated from her; the second officer who greeted the heiress during that boarding says she was unaccompanied.
She can think of no one else who has seen her husband.
The captain asks whether the husband may have left the ship and orders it searched, to no avail.
The other woman tells the doctor that the heiress had admitted waving to nobody at the ship's departure, which they find odd.
Eventually, the crew suspect the heiress is delusional.
That night, the husband phones the heiress with a cryptic warning that they are in danger and to trust no one; he then hangs up.
The doctor gets her to open up about the recent death of her father, a wealthy steel executive.

When the heiress's company's managing director, doctor and servants respond to inquiry that they are unaware of a husband and she is unmarried, the doctor suggests to the heiress that her wedding was wishful thinking.
She explains that the husband wanted a quick, quiet ceremony.
Her uncle might scheme to get her large inheritance that includes her father's company; thus, she kept the marriage secret.
That evening, the husband phones again, asking the heiress to meet him on deck.
They meet only briefly because they hear others approach and the husband runs into the fog, after telling the heiress to meet him again later.
The heiress chases him but ends up in the ship's crowded ballroom, where she goes into hysterics.
The captain demands she be locked in her cabin.
The doctor attends to the ship's third mate, the sailor, who has been confined to his cabin with illness since the ship's departure.
Known only to his accomplice the maid, the sailor is the missing husband, who has faked illness to conceal himself in his quarters.
To inherit her fortune as her husband, he has schemed to make the heiress seem insane and plans to ultimately fake her suicide.
When the sailor learns the heiress has been locked up, he tells the maid to facilitate her escape.
The maid “accidentally” leaves the door unlocked as she checks in on the heiress.
The heiress slips out to keep her assignation with the husband.
The husband tries to throw the heiress overboard—to look like the unstable heiress committed suicide—but is stopped by the doctor.
In the ensuing struggle, the husband falls over the side.
The captain returns the heiress's passport and marriage certificate—found in the sailor's cabin—apologizing to the heiress for challenging both her veracity and sanity.
The maid has confessed to the plot.
The heiress and the doctor have developed a relationship; he will be there to help her get over her ordeal.
The woman, an actress known as "the actress" to her friends, is living in the resort town, the country, where she and financier the businessman plan to marry as soon as he gets a divorce.
The businessman's wife the spouse and her brothers control the businessman's firm and have become suspicious of his business methods.
The spouse is unaware that the businessman is the ringleader of a gang that deals in counterfeit gold coins.
In a casino the actress runs into the debtor, an acquaintance.
He claims a need for money due to his wife's medical bills, so the actress offers him a loan.
The debtor, however, is a criminal and in debt to the businessman.
The actress overhears the spouse at the beauty salon and realises the businessman might be lying about the divorce.
The actress confronts him, then angrily leaves and drives her car off the road, leaving it damaged.
She seeks help at the home of the potter, an artist.
The two begin seeing each other, with the potter teaching her how to use a pottery wheel.
The enforcer, a thug who works for the businessman, is pressuring the debtor to repay what he owes.
In desperation, the debtor breaks into the actress's villa and steals a bracelet.

When he gives it to the enforcer as settlement of his debt, it arouses suspicions from the businessman that his lover and the debtor must be having an affair, because he'd given it to the actress as a gift.
The potter proposes marriage to the actress, and she accepts.
The debtor overhears an argument between the actress and the businessman and eventually realises that she believes the businessman has found out about the potter, whereas he suspects the debtor.
The businessman catches the debtor trying to crack a safe.
During a struggle with him, the businessman is shot with his own gun.
The actress and the potter arrive just as the debtor is trying to hide the body.
They tie up the debtor and are driving him to the police when they are intercepted by the enforcer.
The debtor slips free of his bonds and runs for a bay where the businessman's associates arrive with a boat.
The potter pursues him, leading to a running fistfight on the coastal cliffs.
Meanwhile, the police have been investigating the businessman and the actress; a policeman shoots the enforcer, but he is still able to kill the debtor.
The actress and the potter are absolved of all suspicion by the debtor's dying confession.

The producer, a renowned theatre producer, is attending a cocktail party hosted by the viciously haughty and celebrated actress the star and her quiet husband the star's husband when he meets the young woman.
The seemingly naïve young woman, a 20-year-old aspiring writer, says she hopes to make it big in the city.

She convinces a reluctant producer to persuade his wife, the wife—another famous actress, who is temporarily out of town—to agree to the young woman's use of the couple's apartment to write in during the day.

After the producer and his wife return from the airport and find the young woman hanging dead in their bathroom, a variety of people the young woman has recently met in the city begin to reveal deeper and darker connections with her.
The lieutenant, the detective assigned to the case, soon discovers that this apparent suicide was in fact a homicide.
Further, he believes that the producer, who is suspected of having had an affair with the young woman, is the murderer.
The producer evades arrest and seeks clues to discover the real murderer.
The case becomes further complicated when he and the lieutenant independently realize that the young woman's dealings in the city belie her apparent innocence.
The young woman had recently stayed for a time with her uncle and then moved in with a woman roommate, whose brother she evidently had agreed to marry.

A series of flashbacks reveal that the young woman was craftily piecing together a scheme that would help her both to climb the social ladder and to later conceal the identity of her secret lover by falsely implicating the producer.
This mysterious romance is confirmed by an autopsy, which reveals that the young woman was pregnant at the time of her death.
Everyone the young woman knows is suddenly a suspect in the murder case, including the star and the star's husband, who live in the same apartment building as the producer and his wife.
In the end, the star's husband can no longer keep silent and reveals to his friend the producer that he was the young woman's secret lover, but swears that he did not kill her.
Having bugged the star's husband's apartment, the lieutenant barges in and charges the star's husband with the homicide.
The star finally admits that she murdered the young woman for having had the affair with her husband, whom she later intended to blackmail.
The star staged the death as a suicide.
The carnival owner's carnival has come to town.
Its chief draw is a gorilla named the beast.
Each night, the beast is teased by a trapeze artist named the aerialist.
She swings back and forth, just out of reach from the simian's upraised arms.
This frustrates the beast, but audiences are thrilled.
However, the carnival owner, who is in a relationship with the aerialist, thinks the act is getting old.
So he promotes carnival barker the young man from pitchman to performer.
The young man will don a gorilla costume and become the beast's replacement.
The difference is this time the aerialist will fall from the trapeze and into the arms of a disguised young man, who will make people believe she is performing with the actual gorilla.
While explaining the new routine to the young man, the aerialist acts seductively towards him.
The idea seems promising to everyone but the handler, the beast's trainer, who is about to become unemployed.
The young man has a fiancée named the sweetheart, and she is not happy either, fearing the young man will fall for the aerialist.
The young man takes the job nonetheless, as it would mean a higher pay, postponing his plans of leaving the carnival, marrying the sweetheart and studying law.
That evening, the carnival's crooked concessionaire, the vendor, is found dead near the beast's cage.
His neck is broken, and the culprit was a human being.
The young man becomes a suspect when it is learned he once threatened the vendor for harassing the sweetheart.
However, the young man believes the carnival owner, who seems jealous of whomever the aerialist lays her eyes on, is out to frame him.
Meanwhile, someone wearing the young man's costume releases the beast from his cage.
The animal ends up entering the carnival's mirror maze, where the sweetheart is turning off the lights.
Upon hearing the sweetheart's screams, the carnival's crew rush to her aid.
They find her safe, but another associate lies dead nearby.

Despite the attempts to frame the young man, the police believe he is innocent, and as the investigation is close to finding the culprit, the carnival owner voluntarily takes the blame for the crimes.
He was being blackmailed by two of the victims for his role in the death of a carnival performer years before and seems to be jealous of the young man, so him being the murderer is plausible.
The carnival owner gets incarcerated, and the show goes on.
However, the young man later figures out that, due to an old injury he received while performing, the carnival owner would never have been able to break the first victim's neck.
He suspects the real culprit is the handler, as he used to be married to the aerialist, the other person who was being blackmailed for the performer's death.
As the aerialist's act starts, the young man confronts the handler.
However, the young man quickly notices signs that the aerialist was the one using his costume and realizes she is the killer.
Meanwhile, believing she is performing with a disguised young man, the aerialist lets herself fall into the beast's arms.
While she realizes her mistake, the beast carries a screaming aerialist to the top of the carnival's roller coaster.
Using fireworks, the young man and the police make the gorilla drop the aerialist safely by its side before it dies in a hail of bullets.
As the aerialist is led away by police, the young man and the sweetheart resolve to quit the carnival.
